verses.1: As the LORD said, “Go, and buy for yourself some fresh spices. Put them on your offerings. Do not bring them into the water.”
verses.2: And I will take this place according to the word of Jehovah, and I will set it upon my gifts.
verses.3: And the word of Jehovah was spoken to me once again.
verses.4: Take that portion of the land that you have purchased, which was given to you as a gift. Then go and bury it there, in the hollow of the tree trunk.
verses.5: And I went and washed him in the river Phrat, as Jehovah commanded me.
verses.6: After many days, Jehovah said to me, “Get up and go to Phatta. Take with you that portion of land which I have commanded you to place there.”
verses.7: And I will go and pick up the remains from the place where they were buried. But behold, the remains cannot be used for anything at all.
verses.8: And the word of Jehovah was to me:
verses.9: So said the LORD: Thus shall I destroy the pride of Judah and the pride of Jerusalem.
verses.10: This evil people refuse to listen to my words. They go after other gods to worship them and serve them. And it was at that time that nothing could be done about them.
verses.11: For just as that region became bound to the promises of man, so too I have bound all the houses of Israel and all the houses of Judah to me. May Jehovah make them my people, my name, my praise, and my glory, and not let them be destroyed.
verses.12: And you said to them these words, as the Lord God of Israel said: “All thorns will be covered with oil.” They said to you, “We do not know. We do not understand how all thorns will be covered with oil.”
verses.13: And you said to them, “Thus says the LORD: I will fill all the inhabitants of this land with my people. I will also fill the thrones of David with his kings. I will fill the priests and prophets, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem.”
verses.14: And they will be destroyed together. Their brothers, fathers, and sons will all be destroyed together. The LORD says, “They shall not be united or join together; they shall not live together with those who destroy them.”
verses.15: Hear and listen! Do not be stubborn, for the LORD has spoken.
verses.16: Give honor to Jehovah your God before he is destroyed and before his feet are placed on the mountains of destruction. Let him be lighted up with glory, and let his throne be a shadow for those who seek refuge under it.
verses.17: And if you do not listen in secret, then my soul will weep from before the enemy. My eyes will be filled with tears, for the Lord’s judgment has been pronounced upon me.
verses.18: Say to the king and to the nobles, “Be quiet! For from among your women, shame will come down upon you.”
verses.19: The cities of the Negev were closed, and the gates of Judah were not opened at all. It was a time of darkness for the people of Judah.
verses.20: Look with your eyes, and see those who come from afar. What kind of gift has God given you? You have been given beautiful sheep.
verses.21: What shall I say? It will be a burden upon you. And you will have to bear them upon your shoulders. They will hold you tightly, like fire that burns you down.
verses.22: And if you say in your heart, “How can I call them my friends?” Then they will be revealed to you. Their faces will be shown to you, and they will follow you.
verses.23: May it be that Kushi’s city will be turned into a ruin, and his friends will also be destroyed. Then, you too will be able to do the same to your enemies.
verses.24: And spread them out like threads that can be carried by the wind from one place to another.
verses.25: This is a curse from me, from my mouth. It’s the word of Jehovah, who has forgotten about you and who has trusted in your lies.
verses.26: And I also exposed your secrets in front of you. It seems like you’re quite easy to deceive.
verses.27: Your drunkenness and your wild behavior are a source of shame for you. I saw your shame in the fields. Oh, Jerusalem! Do not be ashamed after your death.
